row1.text: Inventory — simplified, one picture per question

brief.text:
WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY IT IS SIMPLER

The first pass added instruments to the existing screen. This one takes things away until what is left reads at a glance, and it says things in figures rather than charts.

FOUR TILES, FIGURES ONLY. Shelf value with its 30-day change, and what was there 30 days ago beside what is held for others. Shelf health as four counts, each a filter. Buy now and Dead money each name the three lines that matter most, with days left or days since a sale.

ONE ROW OF TOOLS. Search, a state filter whose dots match the health counts, category, sort.

ONE TABLE, ONE OPEN LINE. Five columns, paginated, with a dated "Runs out 13 Sep" pill on every row. Pressing a row opens it on the right: days until empty, a three-step ladder (shelf, floor, cover), four figures, the pace (a day, a week, 30 days), and three actions side by side.

CONSIGNMENT. Goods held for others sit on the shelf and can be sold, but are never counted in the shelf's value. Held lines carry a tag and say how many are yours and how many theirs; a consigned line opened shows ownership and offers settling and returning; Movements has a Consignment kind.

MOVEMENTS. In and out week by week in money at cost, because bags, rolls and boxes do not add up. Each log row shows the kind as a tinted badge (sale, receipt, count, write-off, consignment), the line with its picture, who and which document caused it, the change, the shelf before and after, and the cost.

THE DIALOGS. Count the shelf is a count sheet: pick a scope, type what you see, the record fills in the difference and its cost, and only the lines you count are saved. Receive stacks the suppliers as cards and has one switch for bags or pallets that price and total follow. Correct the count and Change the floor are each one question, one figure, one button.
